chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, who said:

I read in a man’s letter to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: Are the two rakʿahs before salat al-fajr part of salat al-layl, or are they part of the prayer of the day? And at what time should I perform them? So he wrote in his own handwriting: Insert them into salat al-layl as an insertion.

key_terms.احْشُوهُمَا: place them within or insert them
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَانِ: the two units of prayer being asked about
key_terms.حَشْوًا: as an insertion; integrated into the sequence
key_terms.صَلَاةِ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer, within which these two rakʿahs are to be included
key_terms.صَلَاةِ النَّهَارِ: the daytime prayer, contrasted here with the night prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ: the dawn prayer before which these two rakʿahs are performed
key_terms.وَقْتٍ: the specific time at which the prayer should be performed

ai.seo_question: Are the two rakʿahs before salat al-fajr considered part of salat al-layl, and when should they be prayed?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of the two rakʿahs performed before salat al-fajr and clarifies their placement. Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام states that they are to be included within salat al-layl, indicating their association with the night prayer rather than the daytime prayer.
